uncited: **Inputs:** Raw 3D dataset (single byte per voxel), user-specified error tolerance $E_{tol}$, number of processors $P$, caching limits (memory $M_{cache}$, disk $D_{cache}$).
**Wavelet Tree:** Hierarchical structure where leaf nodes are blocks of size $n = 128 \times 128 \times 64$ voxels (1 MB uncompressed).
**Distribution Units:** The tree is partitioned into units along a Hilbert space-filling curve.
Each processor is assigned a set of units.
**Hierarchy Construction:** Collect low-pass filtered subblocks from eight adjacent leaf nodes and group them into a single block of $n$ voxels, forming the low-resolution data for the parent node.
**Error Metric Calculation:** Calculate a hierarchical error metric $E$ for each node.
*   Retrieve the low-pass filtered subblock of size $n/8$ from the parent node.
Tree traversal is $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of nodes, but pruning by error tolerance reduces effective $N$.
**When not to use:** Small datasets where overhead of distribution and tree traversal outweighs benefits; scenarios requiring exact single-resolution rendering without error tolerance control.
